pr.title: Expand the hidden lines around a summary's diff hunks
pr.head: 0a28272ad28fdbe37fd189e52c3811c8170968dc

summary: A summary page shows each changed file only as its diff hunks: the changed lines and the three unchanged lines Git puts around them. A reader who needs the function a hunk sits in, or the lines between two hunks, has had to leave the page for GitHub.

The data half of this work landed in #227. project summary publish now stores the head's copy of each changed file under head/ on the summaries ref. The site build serves each copy once at <base>reviews/blobs/<id>.txt and gives the file a context in the page's data.json: that address, the line count, and each gap, a run of head lines the hunks leave hidden.
This pull request draws that context. Each gap gets an expander row above the first hunk, between two hunks, or below the last. The row has up to three controls:

• Expand down reveals the 20 lines just below the hunk above.
  • Expand up reveals the 20 lines just above the hunk below.
  • Expand all reveals the rest of the gap. Once 20 or fewer lines remain, it is the only control.

The first expand of a file fetches its copy once and highlights the whole text once, so a string or comment that opens inside a gap colours every line it covers. When a gap closes, nothing marks where it was. A file without context, including every file of a summary published before #227, draws no expander. The pull request also marks the summary-diff-context plan completed.

cards.title: Terms on this page
cards.html:
• Hunk table. Each hunk renders as its own <table class="diff">, opened by a tr.hunk header row holding the @@ line.
  • Gap. A run of hidden head lines, start to end on the new side. before is the index of the hunk below it, or the hunk count for the gap below the last hunk. oldStart is the old-side number of start.
  • Expander. A one-row table.diff.gap drawn in a gap's place, holding its controls and how many lines it hides.
  • Context view. What renderSummary hands wireSummary for each file with context, so revealed rows use the file's own column layout.

cards.title: Review so far
cards.html:
• The review of db6f86f was clean, with two suggestions: an ambiguous "It" in docs/cli.md, and keyboard focus that fell to the page body when expand all closed a gap.
  • 0a28272 acts on both. It reorders the docs/cli.md sentences, and it moves focus to the file's next expander, or to the file header, when a gap closes.
  • The review of 0a28272 opened one P2 finding. The new focus move also fires on a mouse click and scrolls the page past the lines the click revealed.

groups.title: The context the page receives
groups.kicker: Types for the data #227 added to each file.
intro: The site build already writes context and each hunk's four header numbers into data.json. These declarations give the page's TypeScript the same shape, so the renderer can read f.context with type checking.

files.note: Adds SummaryHunk, SummaryGap and SummaryContext, and an optional context on SummaryFile.

checks.text: context is optional because a file the build stored no copy of, and every file of an older summary, has none. The renderer treats its absence as no gaps.
The page never reads the hunk numbers oldStart, newStart and their counts. The build uses them to compute gaps, and the type records that the data carries them.

groups.title: Drawing the expanders
groups.kicker: Where each expander goes and which controls it offers.
intro: renderFile builds the hunk tables as before, then places an expander table before hunk i when a gap has before === i, and one after the last hunk when a gap has before equal to the hunk count. Each expander's controls follow from where it sits and how many lines are left:

GapMore than 20 lines left20 or fewer left
Above the first hunkExpand up, expand allExpand all
Between two hunksExpand down, expand up, expand allExpand all
Below the last hunkExpand down, expand allExpand all

The renderer returns a context view for each file with context. It holds the expander and row builders as closures over the file's column layout, so the wiring code redraws an expander or adds rows with the same columns and line-number cells as the diff's own rows.

files.note: Draws the expanders, returns each file's context view, and wires the fetch, the row insertion, the gap closing, and where focus goes after a gap closes.

checks.text: expanderCells chooses the controls: expand all always, and expand down or expand up only while more than STEP lines remain and a hunk sits on that side of the gap.

Each revealed line goes into the page as the highlighter's markup or through esc, never raw. ExpanderTests passes a <script> line through contextRows and gets it back escaped. Verified by reading and by running the test.
The fetch is cached by URL, so two files with identical content share one request. A failed fetch is removed from the cache, so the next click tries again.
The whole file is highlighted once per language and URL. When the highlighter returns a different number of lines than the file has, the page falls back to escaped text rather than misaligned markup.

Closing a gap between two hunks removes the lower table's tr.hunk header and moves its rows into the upper table. Above the first hunk, it removes only that header. Below the last, nothing else. Verified in headless Chromium: expanding every gap of a 120-line file left one table numbered 1 to 120 with no header, equal to the served file line for line.

A click waits for the fetch, then works from the gap's current start and end. Several clicks queued on one pending fetch therefore apply in order, and one that arrives after the gap closed does nothing. Six queued expand downs and an expand all in the browser ended in one merged table.

Expand up, and expand all on the gap above the first hunk, insert at the start of the following table. That puts the rows above the hunk header and above any rows an earlier expand up added, so the lines stay in order.

Open review finding: Chrome focuses a button on a mouse click, so this focus() also runs for mouse readers. It scrolls the next expander into view, past the lines the click just revealed. A 43-line expand all moved the page down 924 pixels in headless Chromium. The suggested fix is to move focus only when the control matches(':focus-visible'), or to pass { preventScroll: true }.

files.note: Styles the expander row in the hunk header's colours, with compact icon buttons in the line-number gutter.
The compiled site/src/summary.ts. npm run build reproduces it exactly.

groups.title: Tests
groups.kicker: The compiled renderer, run under node against a built site.
intro: ExpanderTests builds a site with base /projector/ from a summary with a two-hunk file that has a stored copy and a file without one. It runs the compiled renderSummary under node. rendered_summary now takes a script to run after rendering, so a test can call a context view's contextRows directly.

files.note: Adds ExpanderTests and lets rendered_summary run a follow-up script.

checks.text: The test checks the order of expanders and hunk headers, each expander's controls and hidden-line count, that a file without context draws none, and that a revealed line holding <script> comes out escaped.

groups.title: Documentation and the plan
groups.kicker: What a page can expand, and the plan marked completed.
intro: docs/cli.md and the summarize-pr skill now say what a reader can do with the stored copies. The plan moves to completed, and its outcome section records the evidence for each acceptance criterion and the measured cost.

files.note: Describes the expander controls, after the sentences about what site build reads, and says a standalone site page draws none.
Marks the plan completed, spells out where expand up and expand all insert rows, and replaces the implementation state with the outcome.

checks.text: Section 8, Outcome, cites the tests behind each criterion and the cost figures: 289 distinct files and about 11 MB for this repository's summaries, and under 200 ms for the first expand all on a 5,000-line file.
